title: Fourier coefficient mass of a threshold function
statement: Let $f:\\{−1,1\\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $p:\\{−1,1\\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a nonzero function, and let $\mathcal F$ be a family of subsets of $[n]$. Suppose $f(x)$ is the sign of $p(x)$, with zero assigned the positive sign, for every input $x$, and every set with a nonzero Fourier coefficient of $p$ belongs to $\mathcal F$. Then the sum over $S\in\mathcal F$ of the absolute values of the Fourier coefficients of the real-valued function associated to $f$ is at least $1$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the sign cube
$p$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube
$\mathcal F$ is a finite family of subsets of $[n]$
$f$ is represented by the threshold sign of $p$ at every input
the Fourier support of $p$ is contained in $\mathcal F$
